test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 12 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a fundamental duty stated under the Indian constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**To defend the country.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **“To defend the country” is one of the fundamental duties under Article 51A of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties was introduced by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• It is the moral obligation of every citizen to protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• These duties serve as a constant reminder to citizens to uphold national pride, contribute to the country’s security, and respect its institutions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **To safeguard private property:** The safeguarding of private property is not explicitly mentioned as a fundamental duty in the Indian Constitution. However, Article 300A of the Constitution provides that no person shall be deprived of their property except by authority of law.
 
• **To protect dignity:** While dignity is a core value enshrined in the Preamble of the Constitution, it is not listed as a fundamental duty. The Constitution promotes dignity through fundamental rights, such as the right to equality (Article 14) and the right to life and personal liberty (Article 21).
 
• **To manage religious affairs:** The right to manage religious affairs is a fundamental right under Article 26 of the Constitution. It guarantees every religious denomination or group the freedom to manage their own religious matters. However, this is not a fundamental duty.
